candidates.title: Multimodal Sensing Interface for Haptic Interaction
candidates.abstract: This paper investigates the integration of a multimodal sensing system for exploring limits of vibrato tactile haptic feedback when interacting with 3D representation of real objects. In this study, the spatial locations of the objects are mapped to the work volume of the user using a Kinect sensor. The position of the user’s hand is obtained using the marker-based visual processing. The depth information is used to build a vibrotactile map on a haptic glove enhanced with vibration motors. The users can perceive the location and dimension of remote objects by moving their hand inside a scanning region. A marker detection camera provides the location and orientation of the user’s hand (glove) to map the corresponding tactile message. A preliminary study was conducted to explore how different users can perceive such haptic experiences. Factors such as total number of objects detected, object separation resolution, and dimension-based and shape-based discrimination were evaluated. The preliminary results showed that the localization and counting of objects can be attained with a high degree of success. The users were able to classify groups of objects of different dimensions based on the perceived haptic feedback.

candidates.title: Hierarchical grasp controller using tactile feedback
candidates.abstract: Grasp stability is a challenging problem in robotics. It needs to be robust to external perturbations and adapt to unknown objects. While performing a stable grasp, grip strength control can be a desirable property for many applications. We present an approach for stable object grasping and simultaneous grip strength control using tactile feedback, which is able to deal with unknown objects of different shape, size and material. We develop a generic method that exploits the structure of an anthropomorphic hand to be simple and effective. Our approach uses techniques from classical control theory to develop a controller in charge of coordinating the fingers for achieving grasp stabilization and grip strength control. Then, we applied a machine learning method based on Gaussian mixture model regression, with the aim of further improving stability and increasing robustness to external perturbations. The method has been validated on the iCub robot. Experimental results show the effectiveness of our approach.

candidates.abstract: A comparative analysis of classification algorithms of iCub platform humanoid hand tactile sensors is presented. The experimental data were analyzed with different learning supervised classification algorithms: Decision Trees Classifiers, k-Nearest Neighbors Classifiers (kNN), and Support Vector Machines (SVM). The best result was obtained with a Gaussian SVM kernel, which allowed 97.4% accuracy using 20% data for holdout validation. The results indicate the potential of categorization and learning of robotic hands for object grasping and manipulation.

candidates.title: Dual-arm framework for cooperative applications
candidates.abstract: This paper presents a framework schema that allows to bring simulation results obtained from different dual-arm robotic applications to executions in real environments. The framework uses the Robot Operating System (ROS) to communicate each component of the dual-arm, and the robotic software tool The Kautham Project for the computation of motion paths, inverse kinematics validations, collision checking and the graphical visualization of the simulated environment. The Anthropomorphic Dual Arm Robotic System (ADARS) was used in this work which is composed of two robotic arms of 6 degree of freedom, two anthropomorphic hands, and tactile sensors in the fingertips. The real execution of two different applications are presented to show the robustness of the framework. The resulting framework is general enough, allowing the reimplementation with minimum changes in any other dual-arm system.

candidates.abstract: The aim of the robotics has been, since its beginning, the search of different approaches for supporting humans in complex tasks. Physical human-robot interaction has recently become an indispensable research topic within robotics. Assistance using pHRI has been developed usually with force based controllers that generate a motion from the force measurements. The precise intention of the human is difficult to estimate due to the use of generic sensors that are not able to distinguish between external and internal forces of the system. The present thesis shows the development of a robotic controller that assists in a physical human robot interaction. The work is based in the definition of a dexterous system formed by a robot manipulator and a robotic multifingered hand. candidates.title: Speak2UI: Voice-Driven Low-Level Mobile Interaction Using Context-Aware LLM Command Parsing
candidates.abstract: Touch-based mobile interfaces pose significant accessibility challenges in hands-free scenarios. Face and gaze tracking lack precision for small UI elements. Deep learning-based voice systems depend heavily on training datasets. Commercial voice assistants are restricted to high-level commands. To address this gap, we present Speak2UI, an LLM-based voice control system for hands-free mobile interaction. Speak2UI leverages pre-trained language models for context-aware command interpretation without application-specific training and enables direct voice control of low-level UI elements. We evaluate Speak2UI through two studies. First, we compare its command recognition accuracy and inference latency against Voicify using identical datasets and metrics. Second, we assess small UI element manipulation against touch interaction through controlled user studies in real-world mobile applications. Results demonstrate the potential of LLM-based voice-driven UI manipulation for hands-free mobile interaction. Further evaluation with users from the target population is needed to assess the accessibility benefits of the proposed approach.

candidates.title: T-WLA: Bridging Slow Vision and Fast Touch
candidates.abstract: In contact-rich manipulation, contact conditions can change before a visual policy updates its action plan. Recomputing the plan through the visual policy adds latency, while tactile feedback alone does not specify how the ongoing motion should be revised for the task. We introduce T-WLA, a world-language-action architecture that uses shared visual memory to guide both action generation and tactile correction. At each visual update, the visual branch integrates the current image, task instruction, and retrieved history into a visual memory that conditions base-action generation. The same memory is cached for a lightweight tactile editor, which combines it with the active action chunk and incoming touch to predict residual corrections to unexecuted actions without rerunning the visual branch. Future-image and future-pressure prediction provide training-only supervision, encouraging the visual memory and tactile features to capture interaction dynamics relevant to action generation and correction. We evaluate T-WLA on tactile-conditioned hand-motion prediction using EgoTouch and Tachin, and on four real-world dexterous manipulation tasks. T-WLA reduces finger-joint MPJPE by 30% relative to the strongest reported baseline and achieves an average success rate of approximately 50.0% across real-robot manipulation tasks. Videos and code are available at https://anonymous-submission-20.github.io/T-WLA.github.io/.

candidates.title: GPT-6-Astra Understands Touch and Outperform Vision--Tactile--Language--Action Models
candidates.abstract: General-purpose multimodal models have shown promise as direct robot action policies, yet whether they grasp the physics underlying real-world interactions and can apply that understanding to guide action remains underexplored. We investigate this question using contact-rich manipulation as a representative testbed, examining tactile understanding as a concrete instance of this broader capability. Contact-rich manipulation requires interpreting tactile feedback and adjusting actions after obstruction. Existing learned tactile policies acquire these capabilities through specialized pretraining and per-task optimization, with substantial data and training costs. We present GPT-as-Tactile-Policy, which summarizes expert demonstrations into task guidance and tactile references for contact assessment and corrective action. GPT-6-Astra combines this context with multimodal observations and interaction history to generate control commands and adjust actions through contact feedback. Without additional robotics-specific pretraining or per-task policy fine-tuning, our method achieves 93.8\% mean success across five UniVTAC tasks. Overall performance is comparable to state-of-the-art policies, with higher success on selected tasks. On Insert Hole, tactile feedback improves success from 31\% to 99\%. Execution analysis further demonstrates contact-guided probing and correction, supporting manipulation progress through explicit expert experience and online feedback.

candidates.title: RoboSpan: Learning Modular Coordination Policies for High-DoF Whole-Body Mobile Manipulation with Teleoperation
candidates.abstract: Whole-body mobile manipulation suffers from two fundamental challenges: inherent motion heterogeneity across locomotion, arm, and hand modules, and progressive error accumulation over long-horizon multi-stage tasks. Existing teleoperation platforms also lack integrated dexterous tactile sensing to support coordinated whole-body decision-making. This paper presents RoboSpan, a high-DoF whole-body teleoperation and demonstration platform, and the Hierarchical Modular Framework (HMF) for learning modular coordination policies. HMF functionally decouples the 29-DoF action space into fine hand manipulation, arm pose adjustment, and mobile-base spatial configuration branches, and introduces the Coordinated Modular Embodied Transformer (COMET) with inter-modular cross-attention to enable dynamic information exchange and action coordination. Vision-language model driven hierarchical task decomposition structurally suppresses temporal error propagation, while a full-palm 2D tactile representation encodes distributed contact signals for cross-module tactile empowerment. Experiments on a physical 29-DoF robot demonstrate that the proposed method achieves over 20\% higher task success rate than mainstream baselines across a range of long-horizon whole-body tasks, markedly improving stability and robustness in contact-rich manipulation.

Tactile dynamics provide interaction-aware cues to distinguish manipulation processes with similar motions but different contact states. candidates.title: A Fruit Gripping Evaluation System Based on Tactile Fusion Analysis
candidates.abstract: To address the evaluation requirements for agricultural robotic harvesting, this work presented a fruit-grasping assessment system based on tactile fusion analysis. Four piezoresistive pressure sensors were symmetrically integrated into the inner surfaces of a flexible gripper. A signal-conditioning circuit and a data acquisition module transmitted tactile signals to a Transformer–Mamba fusion network for feature extraction and target classification. After being trained on a dataset comprising 300 samples, the model extracted deep tactile features to distinguish among three target categories: citrus fruits, branches, and leaves. Classification outputs generated control commands for a robotic manipulator, enabling obstacle-avoidance retraction and precise harvesting operations. Experimental evaluations, conducted in both indoor and outdoor environments, demonstrated a target recognition accuracy of 93.12%. The manipulator response time was below 0.5 s, and the operational success rate was 90%. The proposed sensing system and algorithmic framework showed strong adaptability and supported quantitative assessment of grasping performance. The fruit detachment, compression damage, and plant-collision risks were effectively reduced while operational stability and harvesting efficiency improved.
